paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God provides, and He does it one day at a time. The ravens brought Elijah bread and meat in the morning and evening (1 Kings 17:6). Then the brook dried up, and the LORD didn't leave Elijah standing there with an empty cup, because He said, "Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there" (1 Kings 17:9). The LORD had the next step ready before the last one ran out.

The widow shows what trusting that looks like. She had a handful of flour and a little oil, and Elijah told her not to be afraid, then asked her to feed him first (1 Kings 17:12-13). She did it, and the jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word the LORD had spoken through Elijah (1 Kings 17:15-16). I think that was a LOT of trust in a tiny jar, and she didn't get a year of food up front, friend, just enough for each day, and each day it was there.

Then her son died, and the story doesn't hurry past how heavy that is. Elijah didn't give a speech. He carried the boy upstairs and cried out to the LORD, and the LORD listened to his voice and the child's life returned (1 Kings 17:19-22). That's the other half of the lesson: you can bring your hardest moments straight to God, and He hears you. The widow ended up knowing that the word of the LORD from Elijah's mouth was truth (1 Kings 17:24), and you can lean on that word too, friend, even when the brook is dry.
